notes:
Need to search first.I wasn't able to write these notes, because I didn't manage to read any of the sources.

**What happened:** My first try went straight to the Job 20 pages on Enduring Word, BibleHub (Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Gill), Precept Austin and the NET Bible. The fetch tool refused every one, because it only opens a page after that address has come up in a search. I then ran a set of searches to get those addresses, but by then I had used up my tool calls for this turn, so none of them went through. The other tools I have can't reach the internet.

**Why the notes are blank:** Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and leave out anything not found. I read nothing, so there's nothing I can properly report. I could write Job 20 notes from what I already know, but that would break those rules, so I haven't.

**What I'll do next time:** If you send the request again, I'll search first and then read the pages, in this order:
1. **Verse-by-verse traditional reading:** Enduring Word on Job 20; BibleHub and StudyLight for Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Gill, Barnes and Matthew Henry; Precept Austin's Job 20 page.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu); Spurgeon (spurgeon.org); Reformed sources (Ligonier, TGC, Monergism); Lutheran sources (LCMS, 1517). A big question is whether any tradition defends Zophar's view. Most will probably treat it as the flawed thinking that God rejects in Job 42:7, but I'll only say so if the pages do.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible translator notes for the hard Hebrew lines (for example vv. 10, 17, 20 and 26); Bible Odyssey; Catholic sources (New Advent, including Aquinas on Job if they have it, and catholic.com); oca.org. I'll also look for anything these sites say about prosperity or word-of-faith teaching in connection with Zophar's speech.

If you can paste in the text of any of these pages, I can also write notes straight from that, with a URL on each point.
